title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is the opening outline (§1 'Historique') of Grothendieck's plan for a 1976 IHÉS lecture titled roughly 'Complexe De Rham à puissances divisées et ombres(?) des modules(?)'. The marginal list (géométrie différentielle, analytique, algébrique, arithmétique, topologie algébrique {PL, semi-simpliciale}) gives the range of settings where a De Rham-type complex exists. The history runs as follows.
(a) Poincaré's differential forms and Stokes' formula ∫_c dω = ∫_{∂c} ω. Integrating forms over chains gives the map H*_DR(X) → H*(X,ℂ).
(b) De Rham's theorem, conjectured by É. Cartan, is now understood through sheaf theory plus the Poincaré lemma. The line reads, I think, 'but one loses products / torsion'.
(c) Hodge theory adds a bigrading on H*_DR(X) for compact Kähler X.
(d) The Cartan–Serre theorem on Stein manifolds: the holomorphic Poincaré lemma makes holomorphic forms compute cohomology.
(e) The algebraic and arithmetic setting: Dwork, Washnitzer–Monsky, then the crystalline 'yoga' of Berthelot, Illusie, Messing and Mazur. The key remark is that these are cohomology theories whose coefficient rings need not contain ℚ, so torsion is in principle not lost. A later insertion adds that from Weil's point of view, characteristic-0 coefficients had been an 'irreparable defect'. Also cited: Hartshorne, Herrera(–Lieberman), Ogus, Bloch.
(f) Grothendieck's own comparison theorem, algebraic De Rham ≅ analytic for varieties over ℂ, extended by Deligne and Hartshorne to more general coefficients. It gives topological meaning to algebraic De Rham cohomology in characteristic 0.
(g) Sullivan's De Rham complex for arbitrary topological spaces. It uses forms on singular simplices: C^∞, or polynomial with ℂ-, ℝ- or ℚ-coefficients. It computes cohomology with ℂ, ℝ or ℚ coefficients, and there are inclusions C_DRS,ℝ-alg ⊂ C_DRS,C^∞ ⊂ C_DRS ⊃ C_DR.
The next page adds that Sullivan recovers the rational homotopy type (minimal models), 'but again one loses torsion!'. It then starts proving Sullivan's isomorphism via the simplicial cdga of polynomial forms on the affine simplices.
The implicit purpose of the lecture: the crystalline trick (divided powers keep torsion) should be transplanted to Sullivan's setting. A divided-power De Rham complex on simplices would give an integral, torsion-preserving analogue of Sullivan's theory and of rational homotopy theory.
errors: No substantive mathematical errors. The historical attributions (Cartan conjecturing De Rham's theorem; Dwork, Washnitzer–Monsky; Berthelot–Illusie–Messing–Mazur; Deligne and Hartshorne generalizing the comparison theorem) are broadly accurate.

The inclusion diagram for Sullivan's complexes is schematic: the polynomial-forms complex is not literally a subcomplex of the classical C_DR of a manifold except after choosing triangulations. This is harmless as a plan.

missed.claim: Already in 1976 Grothendieck frames the divided-power De Rham complex as the bridge between crystalline cohomology (torsion retained) and Sullivan's rational homotopy theory (torsion lost). This amounts to an early program for integral 'Sullivan theory' via PD-algebras on simplices. It predates Cenkl–Porter's integral forms and the later schematization/E∞ approaches, and the 1976 IHÉS lecture is not generally cited in that literature.
missed.quote: Ici on trouve des théories coh. qui ne sont plus à 'anneau de coeff' ⊃ de car. nulle ... les phénomènes de torsion ne sont pas perdus.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral homotopy-type models (Toën's affine stacks, Horel's binomial rings, Mandell's E∞ cochains) are active topics. A documented 1976 Grothendieck program using divided-power De Rham complexes would be relevant to their history and possibly to concrete PD-algebra models.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is a standard historical survey. The mildly notable point is the dated (1976) framing of a divided-power De Rham complex as an integral, torsion-preserving analogue of Sullivan's theory, seven years before Pursuing Stacks. That framing is only implicit on this page.
transcription_corrections: Title probably 'Compl. DR à p.d. et ombres(?) des modules'; compare the previous page 'Complexe DR à p.d. et ombres'.
Line b) likely reads 'Mais on perd produits, torsion' (rather than 'sans produits').
In e), 'Herrera' presumably refers to Herrera–Lieberman.
